Frequently Asked Questions About Chicago Home Remodeling

Get answers to common questions about kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, timelines, costs, and what to expect during your residential remodeling project.

How Long Does A Typical Bathroom Or Kitchen Remodel Take?

Most bathroom renovations take 2-5 weeks from demolition to completion. Kitchen remodeling typically requires 4-6 weeks. Whole home renovations vary based on scope but generally range from 6-12 weeks. We provide detailed timelines during your free consultation and work diligently to meet deadlines.

How Much Does A Home Remodeling Project Cost In Chicago?

Project costs vary significantly based on scope, size, and material selections. Bathroom remodels typically range from $12,000-$55,000+. Kitchen renovations generally cost $15,000-$80,000+. Whole home remodeling projects vary widely based on square footage and complexity. Wood Contracting delivers superior value without showroom overhead or sales commissions. We provide transparent, detailed proposals during your free consultation.

Do You Handle Permits And HOA Approvals?

Absolutely. We manage all permit applications, HOA submissions, and compliance requirements. With decades of experience navigating Chicago building codes and downtown condo associations, we handle the administrative work so you don't have to. We're familiar with requirements across all Chicago neighborhoods and building types.

What's Included In Your Workmanship Warranty?

Every Wood Contracting project comes with a 1-year workmanship warranty covering our installation and construction. We stand behind our work and ensure you're completely satisfied with the finished results. Material warranties are provided by manufacturers.

What Makes Wood Contracting Different From Other Chicago Contractors?

We're owner-operated, which means Dillon Wood and our dedicated team complete your project, not subcontractors. With 500+ completed projects and an 90% referral rate, we've built our reputation on quality craftsmanship and transparent pricing. We don't have expensive showroom overhead, so your investment goes into your home, not our retail space.

What Areas Of Chicago Do You Serve?

We primarily serve downtown Chicago neighborhoods including South Loop, West Loop, Lincoln Park, Logan Square, Wicker Park, Old Town, Bucktown, and surrounding areas. Our service area extends throughout Cook County from Hyde Park to Evanston. If your home is outside these areas, contact us to discuss your project.

Can I Stay In My Home During The Remodeling?

Yes, most clients remain in their homes during remodeling projects. We contain dust, protect your space, clean up daily, and work respectfully in your home. While some disruption is unavoidable, particularly during kitchen remodels, we minimize inconvenience wherever possible.

Do You Provide Design Services?

We partner with multiple experienced designers, including Emily Andersson Design. Alternatively, you can work with your own designer, or we can help you select materials and finishes without formal design services. We're flexible to match your needs and budget.

Are You Licensed And Insured?

Yes, Wood Contracting is fully licensed and insured. We also meet or exceed all building and HOA requirements. We carry comprehensive liability insurance and workers' compensation coverage to protect you and our team throughout your project.

What If We Encounter Unexpected Issues During Construction?

Surprises occasionally happen, especially in older Chicago buildings. Hidden water damage, outdated wiring, or structural issues sometimes appear during demolition. We address problems immediately, explain your options clearly, and provide transparent pricing for necessary repairs. No hidden fees or surprise charges.

Custom Kitchen Cabinets That Maximize Every Inch

Chicago kitchens rarely have space to waste. Generic cabinets leave gaps along walls, create dead corners with spinning lazy Susans that hold three items, and force you to work around standard heights that don't match how you cook. Custom kitchen cabinets solve these frustrations by fitting your exact space and how you actually use your kitchen.

The Wood Contracting team specializes in custom kitchen cabinets Chicago. We design cabinets that reach the ceiling for maximum storage, create corner solutions that actually access deep space, build in appliance garages and charging stations, incorporate pull-out organizers for pots and spices, and design around your specific appliances and workflow.

Transform your kitchen with cabinets designed for your space, your cooking style, and your storage needs instead of fighting with one-size-fits-none solutions.

Historic Home Kitchens: Modernizing With Character

Lincoln Park, Bucktown, Old Town, Logan Square kitchen remodeling requires balancing preservation with modernization. These neighborhoods feature beautiful vintage homes with kitchens that need serious updating. Original layouts designed for different cooking styles. Outdated electrical and plumbing. Details worth preserving are mixed with a function that no longer works.

We balance respect for architectural character with modern functionality. Updated systems that meet current codes. Layouts reconfigured for how people actually cook today. Storage solutions that didn't exist when your home was built.

What makes this work: Understanding which walls are structural. Knowing Chicago building codes inside and out. Experience with old plumbing and electrical systems. Appreciation for original details worth keeping. Skill to blend old and new seamlessly.

High-End Kitchen Remodeling Chicago: When Quality Matters Most

Some homeowners want a luxury kitchen remodel with every detail elevated: custom cabinetry built to exact specifications, premium natural stone countertops like granite or quartz, intricate tile backsplashes that become focal points, professional-grade appliances from brands like Wolf or Sub-Zero, hardwood or specialty flooring, custom lighting design, and built-in storage solutions.

Wood Contracting's Chicago kitchen remodeling team excels at high-end installations that require precision craftsmanship. We handle custom range hoods, integrated appliance installations, designer hardware, decorative tile patterns, crown molding, and architectural trim details that transform your kitchen into a showpiece.

Our luxury kitchen remodels stand out through meticulous execution: perfect tile cuts around outlets and edges, custom cabinetry that fits seamlessly, countertop seams that disappear, precisely aligned hardware, and factory-quality paint and finish work.

Our Kitchen Remodeling Chicago Process

Kitchen remodeling Chicago transforms outdated, cramped, or dysfunctional kitchens into spaces you'll love cooking in and gathering around. Our kitchen remodeling process handles everything from layout changes to custom cabinetry installation, completing most Chicago kitchen remodels in 4-6 weeks with quality that lasts.

In-Home Consultation

We begin your kitchen remodeling Chicago project with an in-home consultation to understand how you cook and use your kitchen, discuss layout frustrations and what's not working, review your style preferences and inspiration images, assess structural considerations and possibilities, and establish realistic budget and timeline for your kitchen renovation Chicago.

Design & Material Selection

Our kitchen remodeling team works with you or your designer to finalize layouts that improve workflow and storage, select cabinetry style and configuration, choose countertops and backsplash tile, plan lighting and electrical upgrades, and coordinate appliance selections. We design Chicago kitchens that balance beauty with serious functionality.

Procurement & Prep

Once your kitchen remodeling Chicago design is approved, we order custom cabinetry to your exact specifications, schedule countertop fabrication and installation, procure tile and all finish materials, coordinate plumbing and electrical materials, and prepare your home for the construction phase of your kitchen renovation.

Demo & Structural Work

Our team carefully removes your existing kitchen while protecting adjacent rooms from dust and debris, addresses any structural changes or wall removal, updates plumbing and electrical rough-in, installs new gas lines if needed, and ensures the space is properly prepared for your new Chicago kitchen installation.

Cabinet & Finish Installation

During kitchen remodeling, we install custom cabinetry with precision, fabricate and install countertops, complete all backsplash tile work, install new flooring if included, add lighting fixtures and hardware, and ensure every detail reflects the quality craftsmanship your Chicago kitchen renovation deserves.

Final Details & Closeout

We complete your Chicago kitchen remodel with final paint and touch-ups, thorough cleaning and debris removal, appliance installation if we're handling it, testing all systems and functions, and a detailed walkthrough where we ensure you're absolutely thrilled with your transformed kitchen and ready to start cooking.

Improving lighting in kitchens with limited natural light. Creating better flow in awkward layouts. Fitting modern appliances into historic spaces. Meeting building and HOA requirements for condos. Coordinating work in occupied buildings.

We've completed kitchen remodeling in South Loop high-rises, West Loop lofts, Lincoln Park greystones, Wicker Park vintage buildings, Bucktown single-families, Old Town townhomes. Each neighborhood, each building type, each era brings different considerations for kitchen renovation.

You're not getting a contractor learning on your project. You're getting a team that's done this repeatedly in spaces like yours.

Frequently Asked Questions About Kitchen Remodeling In Chicago

See the commonly asked questions Chicago homeowners ask when exploring a kitchen remodel.

How Long Will I Be Without A Kitchen During Remodeling?

Most complete kitchen remodels take 4-6 weeks from demolition to completion. During this time, your kitchen won't be fully functional. We recommend setting up a temporary kitchen in another room with a microwave, coffee maker, mini fridge, and toaster. Many clients embrace exploring Chicago's restaurant scene during remodels. We work efficiently to minimize disruption and get you back to cooking as quickly as possible.

Can I Stay In My Home During Kitchen Remodeling?

Absolutely. Most clients remain in their homes during kitchen remodels. We contain dust with plastic barriers, protect your floors and adjacent spaces, and clean up thoroughly at the end of each day. While it's not always convenient to live without a functional kitchen for several weeks, it's definitely manageable. We respect that this is your home and work carefully to minimize disruption.

How Much Does Kitchen Remodeling Cost In Chicago?

Kitchen remodeling costs in Chicago typically range from $15,000 for cosmetic updates to $80,000+ for complete gut remodels with high-end finishes. The main cost factors are cabinetry (30-40% of budget), labor for all trades, countertops and backsplash, appliances (if we're installing them), and flooring. A typical mid-range kitchen remodel in Chicago costs $22,000-$50,000. We provide detailed, transparent proposals so you understand exactly where your investment goes.

Do You Provide Kitchen Design Services?

We partner with two exceptional local interior designers. Both have extensive experience designing Chicago kitchens for every style and budget. Alternatively, you can work with your own designer, or we can help you select materials and finishes without formal design services. We're flexible to match your needs and preferences.

What If You Encounter Unexpected Issues During Demolition?

Opening walls sometimes reveals surprises common in older Chicago buildings: hidden water damage, outdated wiring not meeting current code, or structural issues. We document everything immediately, explain your options clearly, and provide transparent pricing for necessary repairs before proceeding. While unexpected issues can add cost and time, we handle them professionally and keep you informed throughout.

Can You Work With My Existing Appliances?

Yes, if your appliances are in good condition and will work with your new kitchen design, we can integrate them. However, kitchen remodeling is often an ideal time to upgrade appliances since plumbing and electrical are already being updated. If you're planning to replace appliances within 3-5 years anyway, it often makes sense to do it during the remodel.

Do You Handle Permits For Kitchen Remodeling?

When permits are required by the City of Chicago, we handle all applications and coordination. We're experienced with Chicago's permitting process and building codes. Any permit costs are clearly outlined in your proposal. The permitting process typically takes 2-4 weeks when required.

How Do You Handle Condo Kitchen Remodeling And HOA Requirements?

We specialize in downtown Chicago condo remodeling and are highly experienced with HOA requirements. We prepare and submit all necessary documentation to your building or HOA, coordinate with building management, respect elevator and noise restrictions, and ensure compliance with all building-specific rules. We've worked in hundreds of Chicago buildings and understand the unique requirements of high-rise living.

Frequently Asked Questions About Bathroom Remodeling In Chicago

How Long Does Bathroom Remodeling Take?

Most complete bathroom remodels take 2-5 weeks from demolition to completion. Small powder rooms or half baths can be completed in 2-3 weeks, while full primary bathrooms with extensive tile work take 4-5 weeks. The timeline depends on the scope of work, complexity of tile design, any plumbing relocation, and whether we're dealing with unexpected issues common in older Chicago buildings. Can I Use My Bathroom During Remodeling?

If you're remodeling your only bathroom, you won't have access to it for 2-4 weeks. We recommend arranging alternative arrangements with neighbors, family, or a nearby gym. If you have multiple bathrooms, we can phase the work to ensure you always have at least one functional bathroom. Many Chicago homeowners with one bathroom choose to time their remodel around a vacation or stay elsewhere temporarily.

How Much Does Bathroom Remodeling Cost In Chicago?

Bathroom remodeling costs in Chicago typically range from $12,000 for basic updates to $55,000+ for luxury primary bathroom remodels. The main cost factors are tile work (both materials and skilled labor), plumbing fixtures and relocation, vanity and countertop, custom shower or tub installation, and any necessary structural or plumbing updates. Do You Provide Bathroom Design Services?

We partner with two exceptional local interior designers who specialize in Chicago bathroom design. Both have extensive experience creating functional, beautiful bathrooms for every style and budget. Alternatively, you can work with your own designer, or we can help you select materials and create a layout without formal design services. We're flexible to match your needs and preferences.

What Unexpected Issues Might You Find During Demolition?

Opening walls in Chicago bathrooms often reveals surprises: hidden water damage behind tile, outdated plumbing not meeting current code, mold from moisture issues, or structural problems. We document everything immediately with photos, explain your options clearly, and provide transparent pricing for necessary repairs before proceeding. While unexpected issues can add cost and time, we handle them professionally and keep you informed throughout.

Can You Relocate Plumbing Fixtures In My Bathroom?

Yes, we regularly relocate toilets, vanities, and showers to improve bathroom layouts. However, plumbing relocation adds both cost and time to your project. It requires opening walls and floors, rerouting supply and drain lines, and potentially updating venting. In condos, there may be building restrictions on plumbing relocation. We evaluate what's possible in your space and provide clear pricing for any plumbing changes.

Do You Handle Permits For Bathroom Remodeling?

When permits are required by the City of Chicago for plumbing or electrical work, we handle all applications and coordination. We're experienced with Chicago's permitting process and building codes. Any permit costs are clearly outlined in your proposal. The permitting process typically takes 2-4 weeks when required.

We specialize in downtown Chicago condo remodels and are highly experienced with building requirements. We prepare and submit all necessary documentation to your building or HOA, coordinate with building management for water shutoffs, respect elevator and noise restrictions, ensure proper waterproofing meets building standards, and comply with all building-specific rules. What Approvals Do I Need From My Building?

Condo remodeling Chicago requires extensive building coordination. Can I Stay In My Condo During Remodeling?

For single room remodels like one bathroom, staying is manageable. For kitchen remodels, you'll be without a functional kitchen for 4-6 weeks, which most condo owners find difficult. For whole unit condo remodeling Chicago projects, we strongly recommend moving out temporarily since you'll be without essential facilities and living in active construction. We evaluate what's possible during initial consultation, work with structural engineers if needed, and ensure all changes comply with building requirements and city permits for your condo remodel.

Do I Need City Permits For Condo Remodeling?

Yes, condo remodeling Chicago requires city permits for plumbing, electrical, and any structural work. We handle all permit applications with the City of Chicago, coordinate required inspections, ensure compliance with building codes, and provide permit documentation to your building management. Your building will typically require proof of permits before approving your project.

We take condo remodeling disruption seriously by protecting common areas and hallways during material transport, respecting building noise restrictions and work hours, containing dust within your unit with barriers, removing debris promptly via service elevators, maintaining professional communication with building staff, and being considerate neighbors throughout your condo remodeling Chicago project.

What's Included In Building Coordination?

For every condo remodeling Chicago project, we handle preparing all required HOA/building forms and documentation, submitting insurance certificates, reserving elevators and coordinating delivery schedules, paying required move-in/move-out fees, coordinating with building engineers for shutoffs if needed, ensuring compliance with all building-specific rules, and maintaining positive relationships with building management throughout your remodel.

This Logan Square home had a third-floor outdoor patio that seemed like a luxury when the homeowners bought the place, but reality set in quickly. The patio represented nearly 250 square feet of potential living space going completely to waste while the third-floor unit felt cramped with no home office, inadequate storage, and a layout that didn't work for how the family actually lived. The challenge was converting outdoor space to conditioned interior square footage in an older building with structural considerations, weatherproofing requirements, and the reality that this needed to feel like original interior space, not an obvious add-on.

‍

Our Solution

We designed a complete patio conversion that transformed unused outdoor space into a bright, functional home office and storage room. Structural engineering confirmed the existing patio structure could support interior buildout with proper reinforcement. We fully enclosed the space with energy-efficient windows that maximize natural light while providing insulation, installed proper weatherproofing and moisture barriers critical for converted exterior spaces, extended HVAC from the main unit to ensure year-round comfort, and added electrical with dedicated circuits and ample outlets for office equipment. The new space features luxury vinyl flooring and finishes that match the existing third-floor space so the conversion feels seamless rather than tacked on. All work was coordinated with the homeowner and completed in compliance with Chicago building codes for converting exterior to interior space.

The Result

The completed patio conversion added nearly 250 square feet of highly functional, climate-controlled living space to this Logan Square home. The homeowner now has an expanded space with abundant natural light, and the whole unit functions dramatically better with room to grow. Instead of an outdoor space used 60 days a year, the family gained an interior room they use 365 days a year. This whole home remodeling in Chicago demonstrates how creative space conversion can add serious square footage and value to Chicago multi-family buildings without the complexity and cost of ground-up additions.

Frequently Asked Questions About Basement Finishing In Chicago

See the commonly asked questions Chicago homeowners ask when exploring basement finishing.

How Long Does Basement Finishing Take?

Most complete basement finishing projects take 4-8 weeks from start to completion. Smaller spaces like a single room or home office can be completed in 4-5 weeks, while full basement buildouts with multiple rooms, bathrooms, and wet bars take 6-8 weeks. The timeline depends on square footage, complexity of layout, whether we're adding plumbing, egress window installation, and addressing any moisture or foundation issues. We provide a detailed timeline in your proposal.

Can You Finish A Basement With Low Ceilings?

Yes, many Chicago basements have ceiling heights between 7 and 8 feet, which is workable for finished living space. We use strategies to maximize headroom: flush mount lighting instead of fixtures that hang down, spray foam insulation that's thinner than traditional batts, efficient HVAC solutions, and careful planning around ductwork and pipes. If your basement is under 7 feet, we evaluate whether finishing makes sense or if other solutions work better.

How Much Does Basement Finishing Cost In Chicago?

Basement remodeling costs in Chicago typically range from $10,000 for basic single room conversions to $80,000+ for complete luxury buildouts with multiple rooms, bathrooms, and high-end finishes. The main cost factors are square footage being finished, framing and drywall, flooring throughout, electrical and lighting, HVAC extensions, egress windows if required, bathroom additions, and finish quality. A typical mid-range basement remodel Chicago costs $25,000-$50,000. We provide detailed, transparent proposals so you understand exactly where your investment goes.

Do You Provide Basement Design Services?

We partner with two exceptional local interior designers who specialize in basement layouts and space planning. Both have extensive experience designing Chicago basements for every purpose and budget. What Moisture Issues Should I Address Before Finishing?

Before finishing any Chicago basement, we evaluate moisture conditions carefully. Common issues include foundation seepage, condensation on walls, poor drainage around the foundation, sump pump failures, and high humidity. We address moisture at the source through proper waterproofing, installing or upgrading sump pumps, improving exterior drainage, applying moisture barriers to walls, and specifying moisture-resistant materials. Finishing over existing moisture problems always fails, so we handle this right from the start.

Do I Need Egress Windows In My Finished Basement?

Chicago building code requires egress windows in basement bedrooms for safety. If you're creating a bedroom or guest suite, we'll need to install at least one egress window that meets size requirements for emergency escape. For rec rooms, home offices, or other non-sleeping spaces, egress windows aren't legally required but are often worth adding for natural light and resale value. We handle all egress window installation, cutting, waterproofing, and well installation.

Do You Handle Permits For Basement Finishing?

Yes, basement remodeling Chicago IL requires building permits for the work we do: framing, electrical, plumbing, egress windows, and converting unfinished space to living space. We handle all permit applications and inspections. We're experienced with Chicago's permitting process and building codes for basements. Permit costs are clearly outlined in your proposal. The permitting process typically takes 2-4 weeks.

Can You Add A Bathroom In My Basement?

Yes, adding a basement bathroom is one of our most common requests, especially for guest suites or in-law spaces. This requires plumbing installation which can be straightforward or complex depending on your existing plumbing configuration. In homes with basement bathrooms roughed in, it's relatively simple. Otherwise, we may need to install an ejector pump to move waste up to your main sewer line. We evaluate your specific situation and provide clear pricing for bathroom additions.

What's Your Payment Schedule For Basement Finishing?

Our standard payment schedule is: (1) Deposit upon contract signing (typically 30-50%), (2) Payments at project milestones (framing complete, drywall complete, finishes complete), (3) Final payment upon completion and your satisfaction. Yes, finishing your basement typically provides strong return on investment for Chicago homes. A professionally finished basement adds livable square footage, which directly increases home value. Most homeowners see 60-75% return on investment, while also enjoying the space themselves. For families needing more room without moving, the value is even higher.

Old Town holds some of the oldest homes in the city, built with tiny rear kitchens and additions stacked on over a century, so the work usually opens the space without losing a load-bearing wall or a stack that cannot move. The structure decides the plan before any finish does.

Our kitchen remodeling then installs cabinetry, quartz or natural stone counters, tile or stone backsplash, and appliances, either matching period detail or going fully modern inside the historic shell.

Open a wall in an Old Town bathroom and the age shows: balloon framing, cast-iron drains, galvanized lines, and plaster over a century of movement. We open it and rebuild on a sound base instead of patching over it.
